q1.prompt: Trip owns trip state, Location owns driver coordinates, and Billing owns charges. Who may transition trip 781 from REQUESTED to ACCEPTED?

choices.label: Trip, after reading any location information it needs
Trip and Location may both update the status independently

wrong1.prompt: One mutable fact needs one authoritative owner.
wrong1.explanation: Location can provide data without becoming a second writer of trip state. Single ownership prevents conflicting transitions.

q2.prompt: Two drivers attempt to accept version 3 of the same trip. What should the API boundary provide?

choices.label: A conditional version-3 transition so one succeeds and the other receives Conflict
Two unconditional writes, with whichever arrives last silently winning

wrong2.prompt: The contract must address concurrent writes.
wrong2.explanation: Expected-version or equivalent conditional update preserves one accepted driver and gives the loser a defined result.

q3.prompt: Does naming Trip, Location, and Billing boundaries require three network services on day one?

choices.label: No. They can be modules in one deployable application with clear write ownership
Yes. Every conceptual boundary must add a network hop

wrong3.prompt: Ownership and deployment are separate decisions.
wrong3.explanation: A module boundary can protect responsibilities without distributed-system cost. Split deployment only when scale or team constraints justify it.

success.prompt: You defined the client contract, protected concurrent state changes, and separated ownership from deployment.
